\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Build --- Emit Iter Embed: Results}

\begin{definition}[Run avoiding a state]
\lean{Turing.SafeRun}
\label{Turing.SafeRun}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
Let $H$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean tape symbols, and
state set $B$, and let $c,c'$ be configurations on input $x$. For a state $a\in B$ and a
time $t\in\mathbb N$, the run from $c$ reaches $c'$ after $t$ steps and, at every
earlier time $t'<t$, its state is not $a$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Safety of a zero-step run]
\lean{Turing.SafeRun.zero}
\label{Turing.SafeRun.zero}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.SafeRun}
\difficulty{2}
For any multi-tape machine, forbidden state, and configuration $c$, the run from $c$ for
zero steps is safe and ends at $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Prepending a safe computation step]
\lean{Turing.SafeRun.cons}
\label{Turing.SafeRun.cons}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.SafeRun}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a multi-tape machine with Boolean work tapes and state set $B$, let
$\mathrm{avoid}\in B$, and let $c,c_1,c'$ be configurations on the same input. If one
step of $H$ takes $c$ to $c_1$, the state of $c$ is not $\mathrm{avoid}$, and running
$H$ from $c_1$ for $t$ steps reaches $c'$ without visiting state $\mathrm{avoid}$ at any
time strictly before $t$, then running $H$ from $c$ for $t+1$ steps reaches $c'$ without
visiting state $\mathrm{avoid}$ at any time strictly before $t+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Concatenating safe runs]
\lean{Turing.SafeRun.trans}
\label{Turing.SafeRun.trans}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.SafeRun}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a multi-tape machine with Boolean work tapes and state set $B$, and fix an
avoided state $\mathrm{avoid}\in B$. If $H$ runs safely from $c$ to $c_1$ in $t_1$ steps
and safely from $c_1$ to $c'$ in $t_2$ steps, then it runs safely from $c$ to $c'$ in
$t_1+t_2$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output prefix under one step]
\lean{Turing.step_output_prefix}
\label{Turing.step_output_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean input and output symbols, let $c$ be
a configuration, and let $\mathrm{pre}$ be a finite Boolean word. If the output of $c$
is replaced by $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by its original output, then after one step the
resulting configuration is the same as the one-step successor of $c$ with $\mathrm{pre}$
prefixed to its output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output prefix under computation]
\lean{Turing.runFrom_output_prefix}
\label{Turing.runFrom_output_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.step_output_prefix}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$
be a configuration on input $x$, and let $p$ be a Boolean word. For every $t\in\mathbb
N$, starting the machine from the configuration obtained by prefixing the output of $c$
with $p$ gives the same result as running from $c$ and then prefixing the resulting
output with $p$; all other components of the final configuration agree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output extends the initial output]
\lean{Turing.runFrom_output_extends}
\label{Turing.runFrom_output_extends}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{5}
For any machine $H$ with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and state set $B$, any
configuration $c$, and any $t\in\mathbb N$, there is a finite word $o$ such that the
output after $t$ steps is the initial output of $c$ followed by $o$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs from a halted configuration]
\lean{Turing.runFrom_of_halted}
\label{Turing.runFrom_of_halted}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt}
\difficulty{4}
For any machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input, and state set $B$, if a
configuration $c$ is halted, then after any number $t\in\mathbb N$ of steps the machine
remains in exactly the configuration $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonhalting at every earlier time]
\lean{Turing.state_isSome_of_runFrom}
\label{Turing.state_isSome_of_runFrom}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.runFrom_of_halted}
\difficulty{5}
Let $H$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet and
state set $B$, and let $c$ be a configuration on a finite Boolean input word. If the
configuration reached from $c$ after $t$ steps has state $q_f$, then for every integer
$j$ with $0\le j\le t$, the configuration reached after $j$ steps has some state.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padding a machine action]
\lean{Turing.padAction}
\label{Turing.padAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
For natural numbers $m\le k$, a state map $f:\mathrm{Option}(SS)\to\mathrm{Option}(B)$, and
an action on $m$ Boolean work tapes with states in $SS$, the padded action keeps the
input movement, output, and work-tape actions on indices below $m$; on each added tape it
performs no write and leaves the head stationary. Its successor state is mapped by $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Padded action commutes with configuration embedding]
\lean{Turing.padAction_apply}
\label{Turing.padAction_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.embedCfg, Turing.padAction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $m\le k$, let $B$ and $SS$ be types, and let $x$ be a
finite Boolean input string. For any injection $SS\to B$, any action on $m$ work tapes
with Boolean symbols and states in $SS$, any configuration for that machine, and any
$b\in B$, applying the action padded to $k$ tapes, with its state mapped by the injection,
to the embedded configuration whose state is $b$ gives the embedding of the result of
applying the original action to the original configuration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation of symbols under selected heads]
\lean{Turing.embedCfg_workTapeSymbols}
\label{Turing.embedCfg_workTapeSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.embedCfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m\leq k$, let $S$ and $B$ be symbol sets, let $\iota:S\to B$, and let $c$ be a
configuration of an $m$-tape machine on input $x$. For every $b\in B$, changing the
embedded configuration's state to $b$ leaves unchanged, on each of the first $m$ tapes,
the symbol under the head; these symbols agree with those under the heads in $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output update and configuration embedding]
\lean{Turing.embedCfg_output}
\label{Turing.embedCfg_output}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.embedCfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $m \leq k$, let $S$ and $B$ be symbol sets, let $\iota:S\to B$, and let $c$ be a
configuration of an $m$-tape machine on input $x$. For every output word $o$, embedding
the configuration obtained by replacing $c$'s output with $o$ gives the same
configuration as embedding $c$ first and then replacing the output with $o$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-step run]
\lean{Turing.runFrom_one}
\label{Turing.runFrom_one}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{1}
For any machine $H$ with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and state set $B$, and any
configuration $c$, the configuration reached after one step is $H$'s one-step successor
of $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding a single machine step]
\lean{Turing.embed_step}
\label{Turing.embed_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.embedCfg, Turing.embedCfg_workTapeSymbols, Turing.padAction, Turing.padAction_apply}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m\le k$, let $M$ have $m$ work tapes and state set $S$, and let $H$ have $k$ work
tapes and state set $B$, both with Boolean tape alphabet. Let $\iota:S\to B$, and
suppose configuration $c$ of $M$ is in state $q$. For any $b\in B$, assume that for
every tuple of scanned input and work-tape symbols, the transition of $H$ at state $b$
is the padded, state-mapped action prescribed by $M$ at state $q$. Then one step of $H$
from the embedded configuration obtained by replacing its state with $b$ equals the
embedding of the configuration reached by one step of $M$ from $c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding a computation run]
\lean{Turing.embed_run}
\label{Turing.embed_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.embedCfg, Turing.embed_step, Turing.padAction}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m\le k$, let $M$ be a machine with $m$ work tapes, Boolean tape alphabet, and state
set $S$, and let $H$ be a machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean tape alphabet, and state
set $B$. Let $\iota:S\to B$ and choose an exceptional state $e\in S$. Suppose that, for
every $q\ne e$ and every tuple of scanned input and work-tape symbols, $H$ at state
$\iota(q)$ performs the action obtained from $M$ by retaining its tape operations and
output, padding the extra work tapes with no operation, and mapping its optional
successor state through $\iota$. For any input, initial configuration $c$, and
$t\in\mathbb N$, if at every time $j<t$ the run of $M$ from $c$ is in some state
different from $e$, then the run of $H$ for $t$ steps from the configuration that maps
the states through $\iota$, preserves the first $m$ tapes and heads, and leaves the
extra tapes blank at head position zero is the corresponding embedded configuration of
the run of $M$ after $t$ steps.
\end{theorem}
